clips.title: The story
paras: At Spirit Rock, Canaga Earthcaller guides young shaman through their first communion with the elements. They drink an Earth Sapta on sacred ground to see the Minor Manifestation of Earth.

A sapta is a mystical draught known to only a few shaman masters. Made with elemental magic, it bridges mortal perception and the spiritual plane, granting Sapta Sight to the strong-willed. Because it binds the drinker's spirit directly to an element, tradition forbids drinking it outside consecrated holy ground.

To commune with earth, you leave the Valley of Trials and climb the Hidden Path into Durotar's southern crags. Spirit Rock waits at the trail's end, an elevated sanctuary overlooking the rugged wasteland. Drink the sapta there, and you can perceive what ordinary eyes cannot: an elemental presence among the stone.

The Minor Manifestation of Earth asks no bloodshed or submission. It asks only that you stand humbly before the world. Fire, water, and air bear turbulent, volatile, often chaotic spirits, while earth teaches steadiness. Mountains offer endurance, and plains teach boundless patience.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: A sapta is a drink created to bind our spirits to the elements. Fused with magic, the potion will allow the strong willed to see the elements as no one else can. Your spirit will be connected to the element the sapta was created for, and only a select few adventurer know the recipe.
The sapta is always drunk in a holy place, and never anywhere else--remember that.
Seek out Spirit Rock southwest of here--it is found at the end of the Hidden Path. Drink your sapta there, and... Well, you shall see.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Ah... Friend... Pleased is the earth to have you here.
Bound together in body and spirit, you will go forward knowing that the mountains are your strength; the plains, your patience; and the world itself your essence.

Standing before the earth humbly is all that is required of you for you to pass this rite. But the others are not as passive. They may be chaotic and often violent, but such is the nature of the elements. Dual natures opposing one another, you must come to learn these things intricately.
